open_questions: The specific Oakland EV charger submittal checklist PDF referenced on https://www.oaklandca.gov/My-Household/Building-and-Remodeling/Homeowner-Projects-Permits/Electric-Vehicle-Service-Equipment-Charging-Stations is not indexed directly and could not be opened to verify whether Oakland specifies an EV charger load calculation method or service load factor.

No Oakland-published residential electrical load calculation worksheet or mandatory NEC 220 method (220.82 vs. 220.83) was found on oaklandca.gov; checking the MEP application PDF or contacting the Permit & Services Questions Portal would settle this.

The full Fire Prevention Bureau energy storage system thresholds beyond the 20 kWh single-battery trigger (item 2 in the truncated list on https://www.oaklandca.gov/My-Household/Building-and-Remodeling/Homeowner-Projects-Permits/Solar-Energy-Systems-Facilities) could not be read in full.

The specific Oakland EV charger submittal checklist PDF referenced on https://www.oaklandca.gov/My-Household/Building-and-Remodeling/Homeowner-Projects-Permits/Electric-Vehicle-Service-Equipment-Charging-Stations could not be indexed or opened directly to verify whether Oakland specifies an EV charger load calculation method or service load factor.

The City of Oakland Energy Storage Systems Code Bulletin PDF referenced on https://www.oaklandca.gov/My-Household/Building-and-Remodeling/Homeowner-Projects-Permits/Solar-Energy-Systems-Facilities could not be opened directly to verify additional Fire Prevention Bureau battery spacing or labeling rules.
No Oakland-published residential electrical load calculation worksheet or mandatory NEC 220 method (220.82 vs. 220.83 vs. 220.87) was found on oaklandca.gov.

The MEP application PDF (https://www.oaklandca.gov/files/assets/city/v/3/planning-amp-building/documents/pc/forms-and-apps/application-mep-fillable-online.pdf) lists 'AIC letter, Load calcs & 1 line diameter' under documentation needed for inspection, but does not state the exact amperage threshold at which single-family service upgrades require an AIC letter or one-line diagram.
